quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This makes it slower to respond. You should ride slower than normal, slow down sooner, and keep more distance from other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about hazards ahead.

questions.question: Most motorcycle mirrors are rounded. What do these mirrors do?

options.text: Are easy to use right away.
Make cars look closer than they are.
Show a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they are.
questions.explanation: Rounded mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They make objects appear farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances in these mirrors if you are not used to them.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: How can you ride safely on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the center lane.
Keep your speed the same or go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden moves. Avoid the center of the lane. Follow the tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle clothing should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. It should also protect you in case of a crash.

questions.question: Your rear wheel locks while braking on good road surface. What should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride on the far side of your lane when following another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, drivers will see you easily.
No, drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, passengers may tell the driver you are there.
No, it is illegal to ride anywhere but the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver's rearview mirror will most likely show you.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down earlier than usual.
Wait for larger gaps in traffic before merging.
Accelerate faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate faster than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle and changes how it handles. Expect slower acceleration, slower turns, and need for extra stopping distance.

questions.question: What is the best protection for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Keeping distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.
A good leather jacket.
Sturdy boots.
A good understanding of motorcycle laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Your best protection is to stay far away from other vehicles. This gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes. Wearing proper gear is also important.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time and brake harder.
Do both actions at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.
Do neither action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good tire grip to swerve safely. Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should a rider do when entering a turn?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Move their shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using the brakes if needed.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: The left side
The center
The right side
No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or should always be avoided. Choose a lane position that fits the riding conditions.

questions.question: How do you get maximum braking power?

options.text: Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Get maximum braking power by fully applying both brakes without locking either wheel. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: How should you cross railroad tracks that run along the road?

options.text: Cross at a 90-degree angle.
Never cross the tracks.
Cross at a 45-degree angle or steeper.
Cross slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at a 45-degree angle or steeper.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or road seams at least 45 degrees to your lane. Make a quick, sharp turn. Crossing slowly could catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: Why should you practice with convex mirrors if you are not familiar with them?

options.text: Most people don't know how to use mirrors.
They make objects appear farther away than they really are.
They make objects appear closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to check mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects appear farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice using convex mirrors to get used to them.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks on a dry road, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks on a dry road, you can keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still steer with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handlebar in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handlebar on the side you want to turn. Press the opposite handlebar to return to your original direction after you pass the hazard.

questions.question: To fit a passenger, you may need to:

options.text: Adjust the shocks.
Adjust the handlebars.
Adjust the brakes.
Adjust the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust the shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks before carrying a passenger. The motorcycle will sit differently, so also adjust the headlight and mirrors.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever so the tire can grip again. Then reapply the brake.

questions.question: When it is raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars has not yet washed away. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars for better grip. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the end of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead the group.
